- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.2), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for reversal.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes; if price spiked in last 3–5 days, cap forecast increase at +2% from prior peak.  
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods; if sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.4) and price is above 65, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until reversion.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; if sentiment turns positive after day 15, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day for final 5–7 days.  
- If model forecast is below 60 and sentiment is positive, avoid sharp upward revisions; instead, use linear interpolation from recent low to mid-range.
